Godzilla, Mothra and King Ghidorah: Giant Monsters All-Out Attack (Original Soundtrack) is the soundtrack album to the 2001 Japanese kaiju film Godzilla, Mothra and King Ghidorah: Giant Monsters All-Out Attack, composed by Kow Otani, a frequent collaborator of the film's director, Shusuke Kaneko. Otani created a distinctive score that blended orchestral and electronic elements with techno influences, deliberately avoiding Akira Ifukube's Godzilla style and his own earlier Gamera scores. He drew inspiration from the progressive rock band Goblin and his own score for  (2001).
Otani composed the main monster themes in the unified key of A minor to emphasize their shared mythological essence. Godzilla's motif features low-register brass and strings for a heavy, ominous quality, while Mothra and King Ghidorah are represented by female and male choruses respectively, performed by students from Toho Gakuen School of Music. The end credits incorporate Akira Ifukube's classic "Godzilla Theme" and "War of the Monsters March" from Invasion of Astro-Monster (1965).
The original soundtrack album, featuring 36 tracks from the film score, was released on December 12, 2001, by Tokuma Japan Communications and runs for 57 minutes. In April 2010,  released an expanded edition that runs approximately 75 minutes and includes bonus tracks and demos.
